title: About
text:
This project combines historical and real-time financial data with AI to produce automated research reports for US growth stock investors. By feeding macroeconomic indicators, equity market data, and commodity prices into an AI model, each report identifies historical patterns, draws parallels to current conditions, and highlights risks and opportunities for growth-oriented portfolios.
All charts and visualizations in the reports are created by the author — the AI generates only the written analysis.

title: Market Research
text:
The Late-Cycle Mirage: Navigating US Growth Stocks Amidst Geopolitical Shocks and Yield Curve Un-inversion
Over the past three months leading up to late July 2026, global markets have been heavily influenced by escalating geopolitical fractures, notably the ongoing US-Iran military confrontations and continued strikes in Ukraine. These tensions have pushed Brent crude back above $95 per barrel as of mid-July 2026 and fueled a massive safe-haven rally in gold, which recently peaked near $4,700 an ounce in April 2026 before settling around $4,060 in July. Meanwhile, the MSCI World Index has exhibited extreme volatility, mirroring the late-stage expansion patterns of the late 1990s where late-cycle momentum collides with external shocks. Global yields remain elevated but are beginning to price in the economic drag from these commodity spikes, creating a fragile backdrop for risk assets.



MSCI World Equity Index


The Nasdaq 100 has pushed to an astonishing 28,335 as of late July 2026, while the S&P 500 sits near 7,438 as of late June 2026. This resilience seems detached from the underlying macroeconomic reality. GDP growth slowed to just 1.1% in Q1 2026, and unemployment has drifted up to hover around 4.2% as of mid-2026. We are witnessing a classic late-cycle divergence where equity indices are pricing in a soft landing driven by technological productivity, while the macro data whispers stagflation.



Performance of Major US Stock Indices


The most glaring historical parallel lies in the bond market. The yield curve has officially un-inverted, with the 10-year Treasury at 4.56% and the 2-year at 4.19% as of July 2026. This specific un-inversion pattern closely resembles the environment of late 2000 and mid-2006. In both historical instances, the un-inversion occurred as the Fed faced an external shock or paused easing, signaling the transition from a slowing economy into an actual contraction. The S&P 500 trailing P/E ratio is stretched at 28.5x as of mid-2026, a valuation that leaves little room for a multiple contraction if long-duration risk premiums expand.



US 2Y and 10Y Treasury Yields and Spread


Inflation has proven stickier than the market initially hoped, with CPI hovering around 3.5% and core CPI near 2.6% in mid-2026. The Fed has already brought the target rate down to 3.75% by late 2025, but the commodity shock from the Middle East threatens to derail the disinflationary trend. This dynamic mimics the mid-1960s and 1970s, where premature Fed easing combined with supply-side shocks led to severe multiple compression for high-flying growth names.



Brent Oil Prices


Navigating this environment requires separating structural tailwinds from cyclical complacency. When evaluating the current landscape for US growth equities, we must weigh severe macroeconomic headwinds against pockets of unprecedented technological leverage.

Geopolitical Commodity Shocks & Inflation Stickiness: With Brent crude above $90 and gold at $4,000+, systemic fear is high. If inflation re-accelerates towards 4% due to energy costs, the terminal rate assumptions baked into growth valuations will be violently repriced, posing a severe threat to unprofitable, long-duration tech names.
Yield Curve Un-inversion & Credit Complacency: The BofA High Yield spread is tightly compressed at 2.77% as of July 2026, while the 10Y/2Y curve has un-inverted to +0.37%. This divergence mimics mid-2000, where credit markets remained overly optimistic while the yield curve signaled an impending growth cliff, creating a hidden duration risk for growth equities.
Secular AI & Defense Tech Tailwinds: Despite macro headwinds, capital is aggressively pricing in structural productivity gains. Companies bridging AI infrastructure and autonomous defense systems are absorbing liquidity, acting as the modern equivalent of the telecom boom of 1999 but with vastly superior balance sheets.
Pricing Power in a Commoditized World: With household debt service payments at 11.16% in Q1 2026 and consumer discretionary vulnerable to oil shocks, B2B growth firms with high gross margins and inelastic demand offer a rare hedge. These names mirror the outperformance of high-quality tech during the stagflationary periods of the 1970s.

Suggested Portfolio Exposure for US Growth Stocks: 25-50%
While the Nasdaq 100’s momentum is undeniable, the macro backdrop is actively deteriorating. The un-inversion of the yield curve, coupled with a resurgent oil shock and a stretched P/E of 28.5x, strongly resembles the treacherous final innings of the 2000 and 2006 cycles. At this stage, broad-based growth exposure is highly vulnerable to a multiple compression event. I recommend shifting to a 25-50% allocation, concentrating exclusively on high-conviction, free-cash-flow generative leaders that can self-fund through a potential credit tightening, while entirely shedding speculative, long-duration names that rely on perpetual zero-real-rate assumptions.
